text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPsychologyHow We Decide Who Deserves Our HelpCooperation is a double-edged swordJCBy Jake Currie3:30 PM CDT on August 26, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleCooperation is the bedrock of civilization, but how it emerged from the seemingly selfish evolutionary regime of “survival of the fittest” is something of a puzzle. After all, helping someone comes at a cost, and you may not be able to recoup it. So where did it come from? Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 10 Earth-facing sunspot blasts massive X4-class solar flareShareNextStayOn a small scale, reciprocal cooperation between two individuals (for example, keeping track of who picks up the check when you and a friend dine out) is fairly straightforward. When you scale up that dynamic to include a circle of friends, a classroom, a university campus, etc., things get murikier. For instance, who deserves being helped? How we collectively decide that important question is the subject of a new theoretical study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
